text: Grand Mound is a city in Clinton County, Iowa, United States, with a total area of 1.82 square miles (4.71 km²), all of which is land. As of the 2020 census, the population was 615, with 251 households and 182 families residing in the city, resulting in a population density of 328.6 inhabitants per square mile (126.9/km²) and 257 housing units at an average density of 137.3 per square mile (53.0/km²). The racial makeup was 94.6% White, 0.5% Black or African American, 0.0% Native American, 0.2% Asian, 0.0% Pacific Islander, 0.7% from other races, and 4.1% from two or more races; Hispanic or Latino persons of any race made up 2.4% of the population. The median age was 38.6 years, with 26.0% under 20, 7.8% aged 20–24, 24.2% aged 25–44, 26.7% aged 45–64, and 15.3% 65 or older. The gender makeup was 50.7% male and 49.3% female. In 2010, the population was 642, with 243 households and 185 families, a density of 352.7 inhabitants per square mile (136.2/km²), and a racial composition of 98.9% White, 0.3% Asian, and 0.8% from two or more races; 1.7% were Hispanic or Latino. The median age was 39.5 years, with 24.1% under 18, 10.4% aged 18–24, 23.4% aged 25–44, 28.3% aged 45–64, and 13.6% 65 or older; gender distribution was 50.9% male and 49.1% female. In 2000, the population was 675, with 254 households and 196 families, a density of 367.9 inhabitants per square mile (142.0/km²), and 260 housing units at an average density of 141.5 per square mile (54.6/km²); racial composition was 98.37% White, 0.15% Asian, and 1.48% from two or more races; 1.33% were Hispanic or Latino. The median age was 35 years, with 28.1% under 18, 7.5% aged 18–24, 29.9% aged 25–44, 22.9% aged 45–64, and 11.5% 65 or older; for every 100 females, there were 100.6 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 96.0 males. The median household income was $42,411, the median family income was $46,429, males had a median income of $33,611, females had $20,250, and the per capita income was $17,228. About 4.2% of families and 7.1% of the population were below the poverty line, including 9.6% of those under 18 and 8.9% of those age 65 or older. The Chicago, Iowa and Nebraska Railroad was built through Grand Mound in 1858, and a train station was established. The town was platted in 1866 and named for nearby Sand Mound, a name error due to a recording mistake that was never corrected; legend claims it is the grandest of all mounds. Grand Mound is part of the Central DeWitt Community School District, based in DeWitt, known as the Central Clinton Community School District until July 1, 2014. Prior to the formation of the Central Clinton School District, Grand Mound operated its own junior-senior high school in the same building as the elementary school, with sports teams known as the Cardinals; the last graduating senior class was in 1961, when Grand Mound, Welton, and DeWitt consolidated to form the Central Community School District. Grand Mound Elementary School, which first opened in 1917 on a 4-acre (1.6 ha) property (35 rods, 10 feet by 18 rods), had a second building constructed in 1954 that included a cafeteria, gymnasium, and two classrooms. In 1995, the original 1917 building was closed due to structural unsafety and poor roof condition and was demolished around 1999; after demolition, the cafeteria was used as an office, school nurse area, and reading and speech therapy space. In the 1998–1999 school year, the school had 38 students, and by 2001 enrollment dropped to 35. By 2001, Grand Mound Elementary served only Kindergarten and first grade, and students used the library, media, and computer facilities at Welton Elementary. A bond proposal in circa 2001 aimed to expand DeWitt's elementary schools, centralizing services for the handicapped and closing Grand Mound and Welton schools. By 2002, Grand Mound Elementary closed and was sold to God's Family Baptist Church. After the closure due to declining enrollment and structural concerns, students were bused to elementary schools in Welton and DeWitt; today, with Welton also closed, all elementary-aged students attend school in DeWitt.
